payload.instructions: Consider how the drift affects the target metric.

questions.scenario: An insurer models aggregate loss as the product of claim frequency and average severity.
questions.drift: Claim frequency increases by 10%, while average severity decreases by 8%.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely impact on expected aggregate loss?

solution.text: Expected aggregate loss is proportional to frequency × severity. A 10% increase combined with an 8% decrease results in a net increase (1.10 × 0.92 ≈ 1.012).
